reason: Conversation 2 covered the full expected ground: food safety at 10C, correct identification that the HMCB 7030 is a non-frost-free cooling-plate design (versus Conversation 1's vent-based explanation that doesn't fit the model), checks of dial setting, plinth ventilation and door/cabinet alignment, a full defrost as a low-cost test, and repeated honest guidance that the landlord/letting agent must arrange an engineer if that fails, finishing with a ready-made fault report when the tenant said they couldn't judge the back wall. Conversation 1 never mentioned landlord escalation, food safety or housing ventilation, pushed a 'suitable replacement' part-finder panel before any diagnosis, and simply repeated the defrost instruction without acknowledging the remote uncertainty. Conversation 2's refrigerant-leak discussion was speculative but clearly hedged as a possibility and tied to the engineer route rather than a part, so it stayed within acceptable bounds, though its length and repeated back-wall requests were slightly inefficient.
